title: ZRC Grands Fonds 300 – Series 3
description: A true professional diving watch, born not as a styling exercise, but from the requirements of the French Navy.  Developed in close collaboration with French Navy divers, the Grands Fonds 300 adopted its now-famous crown at 6 o’clock, an instantly recognizable architecture that became ZRC’s signature. title: Tropical ZRC Grands Fonds Série 2
description: There is something deeply fascinating about primitive designs — those early versions where everything essential is already there, before refinement takes over.  This ZRC Grands Fonds Série 2 is exactly that.  Raw, functional and unmistakable, it established the foundations and the visual DNA of every version that would follow. The watch is preserved in excellent overall condition. The case remains remarkably sharp, with strong, well-defined lines and geometry. description: Before dive watches became standardized, there was a short period when every manufacturer seemed to have its own idea of what a professional diver should look like.  The Eberhard Scafograf 300 ref. 11706 belongs exactly to that moment.  Introduced in the early 1960s as the evolution of the Scafograf 200, the 11706 brought water resistance to 300 meters together with a date complication, while retaining the wonderfully unconventional design of the early Scafograf. description: One of Universal Genève’s most desirable chronographs, and quite simply an exceptional example.  This MK2 features the black reverse-panda dial with printed UG logo, preserved here in almost New Old Stock condition. Dial and hands are remarkably untouched, while the case is equally impressive: totally unpolished, with extremely sharp lyre lugs and its original tachymeter bezel beautifully preserved. description: Among the countless Polerouter executions, the Broad Arrow sits in a league of its own.  Produced more than 70 years ago and in extremely small numbers, these early Broad Arrow executions have become some of the hardest Polerouters to find. More than just another rare variation, they are a cornerstone of any serious Polerouter collection. Among all these subtleties, the chocolate dial is probably the coolest of them all. title: Omega Speedmaster 105.003-65 “Ed White” — Restored, made to be worn
description: The 105.003 needs little introduction. Straight lugs, calibre 321, no crown guards and the last Speedmaster case of its kind before the Professional. Better known today as the “Ed White”, it has become one of the most desirable pre-Moon Speedmasters.  This particular example needs a little more explanation. description: The White Shadow belongs to what I consider the last truly fascinating chapter of Universal Genève.  Designed by Gérald Genta and built around UG’s ultra-thin automatic micro-rotor movement, the Shadow family came in three main guises: Golden Shadow in solid gold, Gilt Shadow in gold-plated cases and White Shadow in stainless steel. description: Before the Chronomaster, there was this.  Introduced in 1961, this is the very first execution of what would soon become the Chronomaster Aviator Sea Diver. So early, in fact, that the Chronomaster name had not appeared yet: the dial simply reads CHRONOGRAPH / AVIATOR / SEA DIVER.  And the name says pretty much everything. title: UG Compax 30 chronograph ref 22205
description: Universal Geneve started as a chronograph watch brand. They established the standard of design for elegant chronographs and this almost 90 years «Compax 30 »  is a classic from this era.  The name Compax 30 refers to its distinctive 30-minute chronograph register, rather than the more common 45- or 60-minute counters found on most chronographs of the period. title: Top Time  ref 810 ´AOPA’
description: There are watches that tell the story of aviation through cockpit instruments and professional use. The Top Time AOPA reflects a different chapter: the rise of recreational flying and the freedom that came with it.  Already part of Breitling's catalogue, the Top Time 810 was selected by the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association to carry its identity. title: Seamaster 300 transitional 165.014-62
description: A cornerstone of Omega’s legendary 1957 Trilogy, the Seamaster 300 is an icon of dive watch design — a model that evolved continuously throughout a decade. From the CK to the ST series, its rich history and countless variations make it one of the most fascinating and collectible watches of its era.  This reference 165.014-62 represents a transitional Seamaster 300 — carrying forward the essence of the early four-digit references. title: Datejust 16013 2 tones gilt dial
description: Probably the most iconic Datejust seen in 80s Hong Kong gangster movies — the Rolex Datejust ref. 16013 in its unmistakable two-tone configuration, here fitted with a gilt glossy black dial.  The watch is, of course, in pristine condition, paired with its signature Jubilee bracelet. The glossy dial is immaculate, exactly as it should be.  It comes complete with its original papers, confirming its provenance from… Hong Kong — where else?

title: Seamaster 600 « PloProf » MK4
description: The Seamaster 600, better known as the “PloProf” — short for Plongeur Professionnel — needs little introduction. The ultimate aquatic tool watch, it became legendary through its association with COMEX divers, expeditions aboard Captain Cousteau’s Calypso, and even on the wrist of stylish industrialist Gianni Agnelli, the iconic head of Ferrari. description: If you’re looking for an affordable pre-moon Speedmaster with all the vintage feel and DNA, this is probably it. title: 1984 Speedmaster with rare Télémètre bezel
description: From the 1970s through the 1990s, the ref. 145.022 remained remarkably consistent, evolving only subtly over nearly two decades. Sitting right in the middle of this long production run, this 1984 Speedmaster is often regarded as one of the best-value vintage Speedmasters available today. More affordable than a new one, it offers a compelling blend of vintage charm and everyday reliability. Being among the early ’69s, it also inherits a DON bezel from the calibre 321 Speedmasters.  And what a bezel it is. Beautifully faded over the years, it now pairs perfectly with the chocolate dial. description: Here is a Datejust you don’t see everyday. Produced only for the Italian market, the bamboo bezel is very different from the fluted or the engine turned bezel. It gives to the watch a totally different look and feel.
